## Natural history notes

A medium-sized black songbird characterized by glossy black plumage, a fairly slender bill, and a nasal “uh-uh” or “cah” call that helps distinguish it from the American Crow. In Florida, it is common in coastal areas, marshes, mangroves, wetlands, pine flatwoods, parks, neighborhoods, parking lots, and other open or semi-open habitats, especially near water. It is highly adaptable and omnivorous, feeding on insects, small animals, eggs, carrion, fruits, seeds, and human-associated food, often foraging on the ground or in small groups.
